summary: Michael Puett works in sinology, history and archaeology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1987–1994) studying under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu, and has held professorships at Harvard University (~2001, ~2013).

Michael Pye specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Cambridge (1958–1961), Leeds (PhD), and under Maurice Wiles. His appointments include Leeds (~1971–1978), Marburg (1982–2004), Lancaster (1991–1994), and Otani University (~2004–2007).

Michael Radich works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a PhD from Harvard (~2001–2007) and studied at Kyoto University (2009). He held positions at Victoria University of Wellington (2005–2017) and Heidelberg University (2018).
Michael S. Drummond is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol and was attested as a PhD candidate at Utrecht University in 2006.

Michael Schmidt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held appointments at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1979, 1992, attested 2008), the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (1992), and the University of Göttingen (attested 1995).

Michael Schonken is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned an M.S. in Education from California State University, Fullerton (2013–2015) and became a PhD student at Tsinghua University in 2024.

Michael Sheehy works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies under Steven D. Goodman and has held positions at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia (2018).

Michael Silverstein was a linguist who studied at Stuyvesant High School (~1959–1962) and Harvard University (~1962–1971). He held an academic post at the University of Chicago from around 1970 until 2020.

Michael Slouber is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He has held positions at UC Berkeley (attested 2010), Brown University (attested 2012), St. Mary's College of Maryland (attested 2013), and Western Washington University (attested 2013–2020).

Michael Stanley-Baker specializes in sinology and religious studies. He earned an MA at Indiana University Bloomington under Stephen R. Bokenkamp. His posts include Nanyang Technological University, University of Pittsburgh, Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, and University of Leipzig.
Michael Torsten Much works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg as a fellow and studied under Ernst Steinkellner.

Michael Viggo Fausbøll was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Cand.theol. at the University of Copenhagen (1838–1847). He served at Copenhagen University Library (1861) and held a professorship at the University of Copenhagen (1878–1902).
Michael W. Charney is a historian who earned his PhD from the University of Michigan in 1999. In 2001, he was appointed Professor of Asian and Military History at SOAS University of London.

Michael W. Meister specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Harvard University (BA 1960–1964, MA 1969–1971, PhD 1971–1974) and the University of Pennsylvania (1964–1966), where he was appointed professor around 1976.

Michael Weiers worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He completed his dissertation at the University of Bonn (~1960–1965), where he served as professor from 1972 to 2003, and was an honorary professor at Inner Mongolia University.

Michael Wenger is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He earned an MA from The New School and studied under Mel Weitsman. He was Dean of Buddhist Studies at the San Francisco Zen Center (~1984–2012) and founded Dragons Leap Meditation Center.
Michael Williams is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He has held positions at the University of Vienna (attested 2014–2022) and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2018–2024).

Michael Willis specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned degrees from the University of Victoria and the University of Chicago (-1988). He has held positions at the British Museum (1994–2014) and the Royal Asiatic Society (2020).

Michael Witzel specializes in Indology and linguistics. He led the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1972–1978), held the Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1978–1986), and has held Sanskrit professorships at Harvard University from 1986.
Michael Yorke is a graduate student attested in 2026 at Yale University, where he also holds a post in Religious Studies.
